title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah visits the Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) in Pune and reviews its functioning and progress of various initiatives
subtitle:
Shri Amit Shah interacts with officials and reviews activities related to registration, regulation, monitoring and good governance of Multi-State Cooperative Societies
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation emphasises transparent, accountable and systematic development of cooperative societies in Maharashtra and the Western Region in accordance with the National Cooperation Policy
Shri Amit Shah stresses the need for effective monitoring of cooperative societies and strict compliance with regulatory provisions to prevent potential irregularities
CRCS Regional Office in Pune oversees matters relating to 818 Multi-State Cooperative Societies registered across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
Of the 1,872 Multi-State Cooperative Societies registered across the country, 420 have been registered since the formation of the Ministry of Cooperation
Regional Offices in Pune, Lucknow, Chennai and Kolkata will strengthen monitoring, grievance redressal and regulatory functions relating to Multi-State Cooperative Societies
body_text: In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of 'Sahkar se Samriddhi' , transparency, accountability, good governance and institutional strengthening in the cooperative sector are being continuously promoted under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah. As part of these efforts, Shri Amit Shah today visited the Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) in Pune, Maharashtra. During the visit, he interacted with officials and reviewed the progress of various initiatives relating to the registration, regulation, monitoring and reform of Multi-State Cooperative Societies. Shri Amit Shah particularly sought information regarding the functioning of cooperative societies in Maharashtra, their registration status and measures being taken to further strengthen the regulatory framework. The establishment of Regional Offices of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies is a significant initiative towards ensuring effective regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies and decentralisation of cooperative administration across the country. During the review, Shri Amit Shah emphasised that the development of Multi-State Cooperative Societies in Maharashtra and the Western Region must be aligned with the objectives and guidelines of the National Cooperation Policy. He stated that the role of the Regional Office should not remain confined merely to registration-related activities but should extend to ensuring effective supervision, regulatory compliance, transparency and accountability in the functioning of cooperative societies. The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation also reviewed ongoing activities with the officials and emphasised that registration, inspection, auditing, grievance redressal and other statutory processes relating to cooperative societies must be carried out in a transparent and time-bound manner. He underscored the importance of an effective regulatory framework to promote good governance in cooperative institutions and safeguard the interests of all stakeholders, including members and depositors. The Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) is a statutory authority under the Ministry of Cooperation, appointed under Article 243ZH(f) of the Constitution and Section 4(1) of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002. It regulates cooperative societies whose objectives and areas of operation extend beyond the boundaries of a single State. The CRCS is entrusted with important statutory powers and responsibilities, including registration and regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies, amendments to their registered bye-laws, supersession of Boards in accordance with statutory provisions, inquiries, inspections, audits, settlement of disputes, and liquidation and winding up of defunct societies. At present, a total of 1,872 Multi-State Cooperative Societies are registered across the country. Of these, 420 societies have been registered since the establishment of the Ministry of Cooperation on 6 July 2021. In view of the increasing number of Multi-State Cooperative Societies and their expanding geographical presence, Regional Offices are being established to ensure effective monitoring, regulatory compliance and good governance. The first Regional Office of the CRCS, established in Pune for the Western Region, oversees matters relating to 818 Multi-State Cooperative Societies registered across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. These include 756 societies in Maharashtra, 59 in Gujarat, two in Goa and one in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Thus, a substantial proportion of the country's registered Multi-State Cooperative Societies falls within the jurisdiction of the Pune Regional Office. The Pune Regional Office commenced its operations on 15 April 2026. The Department of Expenditure has sanctioned 10 posts for the office. Arrangements are being made for the deployment of officers and essential support personnel to ensure effective and timely execution of regulatory functions relating to Multi-State Cooperative Societies. To further strengthen the monitoring and administrative framework for Multi-State Cooperative Societies, the Ministry of Cooperation has initiated steps to establish additional Regional Offices in Lucknow for the Northern Region, Chennai for the Southern Region and Kolkata for the Eastern and North-Eastern Regions, in addition to the Pune office. These offices will facilitate decentralisation of regulatory administration, faster approval processes, improved monitoring and compliance, greater financial inclusion, effective grievance redressal and expansion of digital services. The Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies has also undertaken several important initiatives for the digitisation, reform and strengthening of Multi-State Cooperative Societies. These include the development of an online system for processes such as registration of societies, amendments to bye-laws, filing of annual returns and opening of branches. Other significant measures include amendments to the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, computerisation of the offices of the Cooperative Election Authority and the Cooperative Ombudsman, and the establishment of the Cooperative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund (CRRDF). In a significant step towards strengthening financial discipline, transparency and accountability in Multi-State Cooperative Societies, the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Auditor's Report) Order, 2026 (MSCARO, 2026) has also been issued. These reforms aim to ensure better financial management, effective regulatory oversight and protection of the interests of members of cooperative institutions. The visit of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to the Pune Regional Office marks an important step towards strengthening the regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies, enhancing the effectiveness of regional monitoring mechanisms and promoting transparency, accountability and good governance in the cooperative sector in accordance with the National Cooperation Policy. *** AK/AP
